This change is a good step forward for modernizing the EM and removing the global variables.
nit:  can you clean these 'this->' up too?
Done

Can you elaborate on this a little?  You've created a class that's essentially a singleton.  Thats all well and good, and this patch as it stands can probably merge, but what are you thinking this would be used for?  Presumably you can't instantiate multiple instances of EM.

> what are you thinking this would be used for?

Creating a class is a good way to eliminate global variables.

The class instance can hold the variables for the duration of the program.


I will not go into detail as to why we want to get rid of the global variables, i think we are aligned on this topic.

> > what are you thinking this would be used for?
> 
> Creating a class is a good way to eliminate global variables.
> 
> The class instance can hold the variables for the duration of the program.
> 
> 
> I will not go into detail as to why we want to get rid of the global variables, i think we are aligned on this topic.


ACK.  If eliminating global variables is the only goal, I'm in full support (obviously).  "further refactoring" I assumed meant there was more going on.
If we have a class now, why does this need to be static?  Shouldn't this be a member of the EntityManager class?
Done

Every place we do a "this" capture is technically unsafe.  This class as it stands is only constructed in main(), so we won't see the issue yet, but just be aware, these have caused lots of problems in the past.  dbus-sensors had some workarounds using shared_ptr and shared_from_this that we might look into.

Is it fine if we create a ```TODO``` item for this purpose at the point where the EntityManager instance is created in main function?

Something like
```
TODO: The EM instance needs to be shared_ptr and captured via
shared_from_this in all callbacks.
```

Since we cannot encounter the issue anyways, i would not want to go for another cycle since a multiple people already tested the patch.
No, we don't need to have a TODO, I just wanted to capture this here.
can we come up with a better name for this?  EntityManagerDbusState?

Not sure what's wrong with the current name?

We need some top-level class for the class hierarchy and it's common practice for it to have the same name as the containing file.

Agree that there is a slight mismatch between entity-manager and the EntityManager class since the class currently does not handle everything, like acquiring the bus name.

These inconsistencies can be worked out over time.

```EntityManageDbusState``` is for sure misleading since we also hold
json members and not just dbus state.

```cpp
    nlohmann::json lastJson;
    nlohmann::json systemConfiguration;
    Topology topology;
```

> Not sure what's wrong with the current name?
> 

Entity manager is the name of the application, and there are more things in entity manager than just this class.  We need something to disambiguate the app from the class.

> We need some top-level class for the class hierarchy and it's common practice for it to have the same name as the containing file.

Sure, but the argument that we need to name the class something because the file (that existed before the class) is named something is weak.

> 
> Agree that there is a slight mismatch between entity-manager and the EntityManager class since the class currently does not handle everything, like acquiring the bus name.
> 
> These inconsistencies can be worked out over time.
> 
> ```EntityManageDbusState``` is for sure misleading since we also hold
> json members and not just dbus state.
> 
> ```cpp
>     nlohmann::json lastJson;
>     nlohmann::json systemConfiguration;
>     Topology topology;
> ```

Fair.

My convictions here aren't strong.  It's just naming.
